newsitem.title: UK: T&N expects 70 mln from disposals this year.
newsitem.headline: T&N expects 70 mln from disposals this year.

text.p: Auto components maker T&N Plc said it expects to raise around 70 million stg from the sale of peripheral businesses this year to help fund the provisions it has set up to cover its exposure to claims on its former asbestos businesses.
Earlier the company announced it made a pretax loss of 388 million stg for 1996 after exceptional charges of 540 million stg, which included 515 million stg for asbestos provisions and insurance.

The company said the move to cap its exposure to future health claims on asbestos claims gives the group 441 million stg of provisions and a further 500 million of insurance cover against any future asbestos claims.

T&N said when it announced the new provisioning last December that it intended to create a fund to finance the provisions, to be built up over the next three years from free cash flow, external fund-raising and disposals.
Chairman Colin Hope said on Wednesday it has identified non-core assets to be sold, which should raise at least 70 million stg this year and it was not rushing to sell off more.
He said all the non-core businesses have now been identified and he did not feel rushed to build up the provisioning funds since it was still not certain the full amount would be needed.
"This disposals programme is already clearly identified," he told Reuters in an interview.
"Some of them are very good businesses and therefore will be very interesting businesses to sell and indeed discussions are already proceeding in more than one case," he said.

"We certainly very strongly...feel that it would not be in the interests of the shareholders if (disposals) would be in any sense damaging the very very unique and coherent product portfolio that we have built up in our mainstream business," he said.
"I think it would be imprudent...to plan where the full 200 million stg and the next 200 million stg (of the provisions) is coming from."
"We have got three years to do it. The money won't be needed in that period; so let's take it step by step."

Hope said there would be big savings in the provisions if the U.S. Supreme Court backs the former asbestos industry's appeal to be allowed to continue settling all claims under the Georgine class action procedure.
The Supreme Court is expected to give its ruling on the appeal from the industry by June.

"The way we have done the provisioning at the moment we have assumed the Georgine appeal fails....If it doesn't there is about 100 million stg less possibly needed than we previously thought," he said.
